## Directional accuracy

Scorecard common executable next-open-to-close accuracy: 149/318 (46.86%) original, 149/318 (46.86%) candidate. Flat calls abstain; coverage 11.87%; same-active-bar majority baseline 50.00%. Ties count as incorrect in this common diagnostic.

Native forecast reporting uses a different interval boundary and excludes ties. Its old/new percentages change because the label changed from previous-close to executable next-open. That is a measurement correction, not an improved signal. Exact native panels are retained in the JSON.

All 46 scorecard components have coverage records in the JSON. Components requiring absent auxiliary inputs or prospective history are gaps. Gates do not make directional predictions.

Unchanged auxiliary copies should produce parity; this does not establish independent engine agreement.
Auxiliary mechanisms did not receive all 273 DSO passes; no full convergence claim.
Realized-fill win rate is not episode win rate. No suitable directional accuracy for resting-order bots.

Exact configs, inputs, source hashes, errors and indicator accuracy denominators are in auxiliary.json.

readme-f3f98bf0.body:
# Strategy comparison experiment — 2026-11-09

Research output, not investment advice; simulation only.

The baseline comes from source commit 898f09611dc65fd8e8457ced29ac05e0b87568db.
The experiment preserves all 34 registered default strategies, all core simulators,
all strategy cards, and research-only strategy specifications. It changes no live
strategy, service, wallet configuration, default parameter, or production registry.

`original.zip` and `candidate.zip` contain complete, separate source trees. They
expand to `original/` and `candidate/` beside this file on the first comparison or
test. The expanded trees remain on disk. Archives avoid indexing thousands of
identical copies in the repository's generated text index. `archives.json` binds
every member and archive by SHA-256. `snapshot.json` binds the baseline to its source
commit. Expansion verifies all members, refuses unsafe archive paths and refuses
to overwrite an altered source tree.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, with the backtester requirements installed:

```sh
python3 research/strategy_compare.py --contiguous-tail
python3 research/strategy_aux_compare.py
python3 -m unittest backtester.tests.test_strategy_candidate backtester.tests.test_candidate_auxiliary backtester.tests.test_strategy_compare -v
```

The current local Python environment is `[local artifact not published]`.
Data remains in the main checkout's gitignored cache. Result manifests record its
hashes and exact selected periods. A later cache revision is a different experiment.
No command above fetches market data or places orders.

## Read the results

- `results/comparison.md`: all registry strategies, original versus candidate.
- `results/comparison.csv`: signed differences, including accuracy and risk metrics.
- `results/results.json`: complete metric values, accuracy counts and coverage.
- `results/manifest.json`: source hashes, data hashes, splits and execution costs.
- `results/auxiliary.md` and `results/auxiliary.json`: non-registry simulators and indicators.
- `results/initial-gapped-run/`: the retained initial attempt that refused hourly gaps.
- `audit_integrity.md` and `audit_realism.md`: all 273 DSO method statuses and findings.

The comparison uses the same execution engine and costs for both registry variants.
It scores working and temporal holdout periods with fresh capital, causal pre-roll,
and no position carried across the split. The hourly cache has gaps. The explicit
`--contiguous-tail` rule chooses the latest regular suffix by timestamps, before
examining returns, and never interpolates a price or compresses a missing interval.
The original full-cache failure remains visible.

Directional accuracy means signal at close t versus next-bar open-to-close direction.
Flat calls abstain. Active-call counts, coverage and the same-sample majority baseline
matter as much as the percentage. Default registry strategies are long/flat; a high
hit rate can simply reflect bullish bars. Realized-event win rate includes partial
resizes and is not a count of independent round trips. Costed returns, drawdown,
Sharpe and fees are separate measurements. The auxiliary scorecard's native old/new
accuracy changes partly because the defect fix corrects its label; its executable
common-label comparison distinguishes this from a forecasting improvement.

This is the DSO defect track. No parameter search or promotion ran. Historical data
and defaults were previously researched; temporal holdout results are exploratory,
not independent confirmation. Missing robustness, significance, live-fill and data
inputs are explicitly unresolved. The audit does not claim CLEAN convergence or a
validated profitable strategy. Research-only specifications cannot be executed.

## Restore candidate copies

This does not change production. To restore distributed candidates after local edits:

```sh
mv research/strategy_experiment/candidate /tmp/strategy-candidate-before-restore
python3 -c 'from research.strategy_snapshots import ensure_snapshots; ensure_snapshots()'
```

report-d2b7681e.body:
# Before and after DSO

Research output, not investment advice; simulation only.

**No measured forecasting improvement.** All 34 registered strategies have identical
before/after directional accuracy on each of the four matched datasets. The two
hourly sizing corrections produce worse net returns on the evaluated temporal
holdout. The experiment leaves the originals and the production registry unchanged.

| Hourly SOL strategy | Directional accuracy old → new | Net return old → new | Sharpe old → new | Maximum drawdown old → new |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Volatility target | 46.02% → 46.02% | −11.50% → −12.24% | −2.172 → −2.436 | −24.22% → −24.01% |
| EWMA volatility target | 46.02% → 46.02% | −11.50% → −12.43% | −2.172 → −2.474 | −24.22% → −23.79% |

These are comparisons of corrected economics, not promotions. More realistic
sizing also creates additional resize events and fees. Daily strategy results
remain identical. The hourly tail has 4,410 contiguous real bars; its final 1,323
bars form the evaluation segment. No missing prices were synthesized. The initial
whole-cache refusal remains in `results/initial-gapped-run/`.

## Scope and evidence

- 34 registry defaults × 4 datasets × 2 variants × 2 temporal splits = 544 completed evaluations, zero failed cells in the final run.
- All original core modules, cards and research-only specifications are preserved in 1,822 checksum-bound files. The candidate has 1,823 files, including the cadence helper.
- Auxiliary ladder-grid and DCA simulations ran on all four datasets. Both paired-spread simulations ran and took zero trades. The completed-day triangle replay ran; its small executed-cycle sample is insufficient evidence of an edge. All unchanged mechanisms produced parity.
- The scorecard comparison records all 46 components: 38 can run with the supplied OHLCV data and 8 need missing inputs. Common executable accuracy is 149/318 = 46.86% for both variants, with 11.87% coverage and a 50% active-sample majority baseline.
- The scorecard's native reported accuracy changed from 48.68% to 49.50% because its outcome label was corrected. This is a measurement correction, not improved predictions. Its adaptive learner retains its documented close-to-close target; the report flags that mismatch.
- Research-only specifications and data-dependent components remain explicitly non-executable or insufficiently evidenced. No losing configuration was removed.

## Defects corrected in candidate copies

| Finding | Severity | Correction | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily risk annualizer used on hourly bars | Critical | Infer periods per year from visible timestamps for the two volatility-target rules | Daily parity; hourly size ratio sqrt(24); prefix invariance; invalid cadence refusal |
| Cards call the faulty hourly degeneracy valid | High | Retire the faulty interpretation in the two candidate cards | Original cards preserved; archive/hash checks |
| Scorecard reports close-to-close accuracy and net returns as executable | Critical | Score diagnostics from next open to next close and state label basis | Gap example changes 100% false success to 0%; same executable horizon net figure |
| Triangle replay accepts future quote timestamps | Critical | Require finite quote time and nonnegative bounded quote age | Future, stale and nonfinite quotes refused; current quotes still accepted |

## DSO status and metric panel

The two audit bundles enumerate all 273 registry method rows across DI/OV/ST/RR/RB/CE/RA/IF/RP.
Their statuses distinguish executed or static checks, inapplicable methods, missing
inputs, and venue/live-data gaps. Auxiliary review is additional scoped coverage,
not a claim that every method ran for every auxiliary mechanism.

One defect-remediation iteration was followed by candidate regression checks,
matched empirical reruns, and an independent final review. The reports retain
unexecuted significance, perturbation, CPCV/PBO and live-fill requirements. This
run does not claim CLEAN convergence, statistically validated gains, or promotion.
The canonical convergence and promotion contracts are
`[local artifact not published]` and
`[local artifact not published]`.

Computed registry metrics include active accuracy/count/coverage/base rate, realized-event
win rate and count, return, CAGR, Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, volatility, profit factor,
average win/loss, drawdown and duration, exposure, fees, borrow costs, liquidations,
and equity. Undefined values are JSON null. Full values and conventions are in
`results/results.json`; signed comparisons are in `results/comparison.csv`.
Other metric-only methods requiring resampling, additional labels or source data
remain insufficient evidence. Annualized short-window metrics are descriptive.

## Verification and reproducibility

The baseline backtester suite ran 941 tests with one generated-index failure after
workflow records changed. No strategy test failed. The final suite passed all 960 tests. The independent final reviewer found no
corroborated Medium+ source or provenance defects. Documentation/index gates and
archive-number verification are recorded in `memory.md`. The comparison manifests bind source packages,
runner, common engine, cached inputs, selected periods, costs and splits. Both
source packages remained unchanged during evaluation. Archives verify and expand
in a fresh directory and reject an altered expanded source tree.

No parameter search ran. Historical data and defaults were examined in earlier
research; this temporal split is exploratory rather than independent confirmation.
Accuracy does not establish profitability. These losing corrected results provide
no basis to replace production strategies.

## Rollback

The source archives and original source hash map permit exact recovery. Restore the
candidate distribution without touching production:

```sh
mv research/strategy_experiment/candidate /tmp/strategy-candidate-before-restore
python3 -c 'from research.strategy_snapshots import ensure_snapshots; ensure_snapshots()'
```

# TradingView Channel Breakout: source contract and open research

Version: 0.1.0. Delta: record v29 source intent semantics and limitations.

The user's screenshot names Channel Breakout, a distinct built-in from Price
Channel. This is a draft research contract, not a TradingView parity proof or
completed rabbithole. TradingView Pine v6 v29 source `src:76a6738dbe0a2319`,
SHA-256 `f438bd98aefb5ed835939a63678dd707740f2265459bd19923ce12c9b056cf30`:
https://pine-facade.tradingview.com/pine-facade/get/STD%3BChannel%251BreakOut%251Strategy/last

Default length is 5. At each bar close the source uses the trailing high and
low, including the current bar. It places a long stop one tick above the high
only when `close[length]` exists. It places a short stop one tick below the low
outside that guard. The unguarded short can be submitted before six complete
bars exist; do not impose the long guard on both sides. Neither order is
explicitly cancelled in this source. Quantity and fill rules are separate.
The adapter accepts complete finite positive bars and refuses invalid extrema;
it does not claim Pine missing-value equivalence.

The matched Coinbase perpetual tape, exact tester properties, quantity, costs,
funding and margin are unknown. The user's screenshot is an observation of a
TradingView report and is not independently reproduced by a Jupiter oracle
proxy. Complete family/queue dedup, measured depth, independent negation and
trusted finalization remain open. Check fresh protected intervals before every
simulation and refuse reserved data.

# TradingView Momentum: source contract and open research

Version: 0.1.0. Delta: record the pinned built-in and a draft intent adapter.

Status: research and parity are incomplete. This is an execution-contract
extension for the existing research-only `tv_43000599883_momentum_strategy`
card, not a replacement of its checksum-bound record or a claim of profitability.

## Mechanism and order intents

The TradingView Pine v6 Momentum built-in v29.0 snapshot is Mongo source
`src:226ef9fa1b185243`, SHA-256
`c1ffb758acd11d4a6c98142e370b8059f23ca4e0281f06d4eeb34062651f80f8`:
https://pine-facade.tradingview.com/pine-facade/get/STD%3BMomentum%251Strategy/last
The `last` URL can change; the snapshot identifies the version studied.

With close C and default length 12, M[t] = C[t] - C[t-12] and
D[t] = M[t] - M[t-1]. At a bar close, if M > 0 and D > 0, the
source places or updates a long stop at high plus one minimum tick; otherwise
it cancels the long entry. Then, if M < 0 and D < 0, it places or updates a
short stop at low minus one minimum tick; otherwise it cancels the short entry.
Equality cancels. The source does not set a quantity. Fourteen closes are
needed for the first complete default-length calculation. A valid signal is an
order intent, not proof of a fill. The intent adapter emits these actions in
source order and requires explicit market tick size.

TradingView's official Momentum help describes directional change, but does
not by itself specify the stop orders or prove a trading result:
https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000599883-momentum-strategy/

The official emulator documentation says default orders fill no earlier than the
next available tick, price-based orders crossed in an interbar gap fill at the
next open, and opposite `strategy.entry` orders reverse the existing position:
https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/
These are conditional on the simulator settings. Intrabar OHLC path assumptions,
equal-distance ambiguity, order modification and cancellation timing require
separate tests against the selected broker model and chart settings.

## Evidence and limits

Hudson and Urquhart's *Technical trading and cryptocurrencies* studies daily
Bitcoin, Litecoin, Ethereum and Ripple, and reports no Bitcoin predictability
in its out-of-sample period even while reporting positive findings elsewhere:
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10479-019-03357-1
Mongo source `src:05f776a75773c4dc`, SHA-256
`82060202e1112cb2261b1fd882a30293261a9133781964f8dec72b3f33abd5fb`.
This warns against assuming persistence; its daily assets, era, rules and costs
do not establish an edge or loss for ten-minute ZEC perpetual Momentum.

The owner confirmed ten-minute bars and default inputs for the named chart,
`COINBASE:ZECUSDC.P`, with a June 21–November 16, 2026 target. Exact matched
bars, endpoint time, historical script version, sizing, margin, fees, spread,
slippage and funding remain unverified. A USD or spot proxy must be labelled
and cannot establish reproduction of the owner's reported return. The shared
OHLC emulator is a sensitivity model, not a TradingView parity proof; it omits
funding, spread, margin, liquidation and venue rejection.

The Mongo rabbithole run remains unqualified. The complete selected-family
census and STOP/queue join, source-floor assessment, independent negation,
measured depth passes, trusted gate and publication receipt remain open. Do not
call the depth saturated or the strategy card executable on this evidence.

## Backtest protocol

After checking current protected intervals and refusing reserved ranges, use a
matched and complete ten-minute tape, record provenance and exact tester
settings, and freeze them before evaluation. Preserve missing candles. Supply
explicit tick size and position size, verify order/fill traces against the chart,
and report assumed path and gap behavior, returns, trade count, drawdown,
buy-and-hold and cost sensitivity. Model or explicitly mark missing funding,
margin and liquidation; never silently set them to zero. Keep tuning separate
from untouched evaluation periods. No actual market backtest is asserted here.

# TradingView single moving average: research draft

Version: 0.1.0. Delta: record source contract and preliminary evidence. This
is not a qualified rabbithole, registered strategy card, or performance result.

## Identity and signal

The TradingView built-in `STD;MovingAvg%1Cross%1Strategy`, Pine v6 source
version 31.0, is pinned in Mongo as `src:d009b1e195649778`, SHA-256
`3f4d5ec22e85d0fb70797001140574a78b73779c50852545f0b76eee7b2f5e68`.
It compares close to a single SMA of close, with default length 9. Each side
counts consecutive closes strictly beyond the average; an entry is issued
only when its side's counter equals default confirmation 1. Equality resets
both counters. A sequence that touches the average and resumes above it can
therefore issue a new same-side entry intent. The existing `ma_crossover`
strategy instead compares fast and slow averages and is not equivalent.

Official historical source versions 29.0 and 30.0 have identical source bytes
(`22405722377b28e8400ed1c1fdb25dd976aa213b7a9d449af8fbbdd0c19f67d9`).
Replacing only the strategy title with the version 31 title reproduces the
complete pinned version 31 source byte for byte. This comparison does not
identify which version was active on the user's chart.

The existing `research/tradingview-card-coverage.json` maps official help
publication 43000599885, MovingAvg Cross, to `ma_crossover` and calls it
`existing`. That mapping does not establish implementation parity: the
referenced code is the two-average 20/50 strategy. The coverage file also maps
the distinct MovingAvg2Line Cross publication to that code. Preserve the
checksum-bound readiness records while reconciling these mismatches through
their owning workflow.

The source submits market `strategy.entry` orders, long `MACrossLE` and short
`MACrossSE`, without specifying quantity. TradingView's strategy documentation
`src:6e1dd8adf7931dc7`, SHA-256
`9367214372491512932d135b9f03bbf123618a981e05598dc955b29c7fc78ecd`,
describes default next-available-tick fills and automatic reversal sizing.
Settings can change execution and costs. The user's settings for this
strategy have not been established; neither default zero fees nor sizing from
another strategy should be substituted as fact.

## Independent empirical context

Hudson and Urquhart (2019), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10479-019-03357-1 ,
report no out-of-sample predictability for Bitcoin in their selected daily
study, while reporting predictability for other sampled cryptocurrencies.
Their study does not test this ZEC perpetual strategy. Deprez and Frömmel,
https://backoffice.biblio.ugent.be/download/01HY3C3S169G1N6QNYR55NZMFB/01HY60XZGZYHNQ6188MSVJT0SG ,
report risk-adjusted out-of-sample Bitcoin results for portfolios of selected
rules with modeled transaction costs; their long-or-out Bitstamp design is not
the TradingView long/short perpetual. The latter study reports no significant
absolute outperformance and greater sensitivity to unexpected costs at higher
frequencies. These findings cannot establish a return for this strategy, venue,
or period. The papers differ in sample and method.

## Reconciliation proposal

Use a distinct source-specific single-SMA identity and card after independent
contract review. Correct the existing coverage mapping through its owning
helper, with its checksum and version gates. Preserve the generic 20/50
strategy and its historical results. Do not register the draft adapter until
the shared order engine, card defaults, schema, and trace tests agree.

## Backtest contract and outstanding gates

The owner confirmed 10-minute bars and default strategy inputs for
`COINBASE:ZECUSDC.P`. Obtain matched perpetual bars, exact date boundaries,
tester capital, quantity, margin, commissions, slippage, processing settings,
funding and liquidation assumptions before claiming reproduction. The
reported five-month return is a user observation, not independently reproduced.
Preserve all reserved intervals. Separately label any permissible proxy study,
including instrument, data gaps, costs and omissions.

The `research/tv_single_ma.py` draft emits close-time intents and deliberately
rejects nonfinite close values. It is not registered, and warmup, comparison
precision, missing-data semantics and complete emulator parity need further
verification against TradingView. The shared offline engine omits funding,
spread, margin and liquidation. Do not equate its traces with venue fills.

## Retrospective proxy sensitivity

The shared prior Jupiter ZEC/USD oracle window contains 41,640 contiguous
minutes from 2026-10-10 21:00 UTC through 2026-11-08 19:00 UTC exclusive.
The comparator uses $100,000 initial cash and $1,000 target notional based on
the signal close. The next-open fill notional can differ. A $1,000 unlevered
buy-and-hold position gained $33.31 before costs over the same window. Fresh
ZEC and BTC reservation checks surrounded each simulation. Open positions
are marked at the last close, not forcibly liquidated.

| Bars | Assumed cost per side | P&L | Closed trades | Max drawdown |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10 minutes | zero | +$570.81 | 731 | 0.208% |
| 10 minutes | 10 bp fee + 1 bp slippage | -$1,038.57 | 731 | 1.177% |
| 15 minutes | zero | +$530.94 | 487 | 0.183% |
| 15 minutes | 10 bp fee + 1 bp slippage | -$541.65 | 487 | 0.721% |

These are in-sample retrospective proxy results, not Coinbase perpetual or
TradingView replication, an out-of-sample evaluation, or live-net results.
Funding, spread beyond the slippage scenario, margin, liquidation, and actual
account settings are unknown. The native result is
`art:023f73b84f69c17606635974140b7cb8003dfcfb36590e0b6ca81017ce3113a5`.

Mongo run `run:2ceb379c607a2a79120f4d92639b671d5a6f9670129529994e098f847a0a7ed0`
remains unqualified. Complete authoritative family reconciliation, independent
negation, countable six-question passes, atomic evidence-bound claims, trusted
gate and publication receipts before any saturation or qualification claim.

finite, positive OHLC input and refuses invalid extrema; it does not claim
full Pine missing-value equivalence. Quantity, fills and broker properties are
separate from signal generation.

five bars, offsets stops by a tick, and guards only its long entry. The owner's
screenshot of Channel Breakout must not be attributed to Price Channel.

quantity, costs, funding and margin are not established. A Jupiter ZEC/USD
oracle proxy comparison is exploratory and cannot reproduce the chart or

census, trusted semantic gates and publication receipts are still incomplete.

checksum or the existing Volty runner. TradingView Pine v6 v30 source

The source defaults to length 5 and multiplier 0.75. It calculates a simple
moving average of true range and multiplies it by the multiplier; it does not
use Wilder-smoothed ATR. Once `close[length]` is available, it places a long
stop at current close plus that width and a short stop at current close minus
that width. Its declaration does not fix order quantity. The isolated adapter
assumes complete finite positive bars and refuses invalid input; it does not
claim equivalence for Pine missing-value behavior. A fixture checks its stop
levels against the existing Volty runner on the next bar; that is not a fill
parity or profitability test.

The owner's screenshot shows a TradingView result, not an independent replay.

and actual size remain unverified. A separate Jupiter ZEC/USD oracle proxy is
exploratory. Complete shared family/queue reconciliation, independent negation,
measured depth and trusted gate/publication receipts remain open. Check current
protected intervals before each simulation and refuse reserved data.
